title: Xanthe and the Hollow
premise: Coral Sandoval, an exiled storm-caller hiding under a false name in the magic-hating city of Vell, discovers his date—a quiet archivist named Wren—in a century-old book of prophecies that names him not as Coral but as Xanthe, heir to a drowned kingdom called the Hollow. The prophecy promises a door out of a country that no longer exists, open only while the last dragon-fire still burns. Pursued by the Ministry of Unmaking and haunted by the mother who exiled him, Coral must choose between the invisible life he built with Wren and the inheritance that could unmake him. In the end he opens the door, lets the old kingdom die on his own terms, and returns to Vell—renamed, loved, and finally visible.
about_author: Cyrus Ashgrove is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper who claims to have learned storytelling from fog and failing engines. They write fantasy about people who inherit things they never asked for.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He sells a luck-knot to a nervous bride, breaking the city's magic laws in increments too small to notice. Establishes his careful invisibility and his growing tenderness for Wren, the archivist he's been seeing for three weeks. Emotional beat: the ache of a life lived at half-volume.

chapters.title: The Date
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Dinner with Wren in a noodle shop; Wren mentions a strange manuscript he's cataloguing that 'keeps writing itself.' Coral feels the old storm stirring in his chest and suppresses it. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by dread—the first hint that his two worlds are colliding.

chapters.title: The Book That Writes Itself
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the archive's restricted stacks, Wren finds his own name beside Coral's in a prophecy dated a hundred years past, describing tonight's dinner verbatim. He photographs the page, hands shaking. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear—he has fallen for someone history has already written.

chapters.title: Xanthe
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Wren shows him the page; the name printed there is Xanthe Sandoval, the name his mother burned out of every record. Coral confesses he is exiled royalty of the Hollow, a kingdom sunk beneath the sea a decade ago. Emotional beat: exposure—the relief and terror of being truly seen.

chapters.title: The Ministry Knocks
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Agents of the Ministry of Unmaking raid Coral's charm stall; he escapes through a storm he can no longer pretend he didn't call. Wren shelters him. Emotional beat: the invisible life is over; the fugitive life begins.

chapters.title: What the Mother Left
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Deciphering the prophecy, Wren learns the door out of the dead country opens only while the last dragon-fire gutters—and it burns in the ruins of the Hollow's palace, where Coral's mother died holding it lit. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance; duty arrives wearing love's face.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Terms
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They hire Ossa, a one-armed smuggler who once ferried refugees from the Hollow's sinking, paying with Coral's last real charm. Ossa warns them the sea remembers its kings. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; the cost of the journey made concrete.

chapters.title: Storm-Crossing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At sea, a Ministry cutter pursues them into a squall. Coral must call a storm openly for the first time in ten years—and finds the power has grown monstrous in captivity. Emotional beat: exhilaration and horror; he saves the boat and terrifies himself.

chapters.title: Wren's Heresy
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren admits he copied the prophecy pages and sent them to a colleague before fleeing—meaning the Ministry will learn everything. Guilt fractures his trust with Coral. Emotional beat: love against honesty; the first real fight between them.

chapters.title: The Drowned Coast
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They land on the salt-scoured shore where the Hollow's capital sank. Ghost-lights of the old court drift over the shallows, and one of them wears Coral's mother's face. Emotional beat: homesickness for a place that no longer exists.

chapters.title: Court of Salt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The ghost-court tests Wren as the outsider who would take their king away. He answers their riddles with archivist's truth rather than flattery, earning passage. Emotional beat: Wren proves he belongs beside Coral not by blood but by choice.

chapters.title: The Guttering Light
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the sunken palace they find the last dragon-fire, small as a candle in a brazier of black glass, tended by a blind firekeeper who has waited ten years for 'the boy who ran.' Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Ministry Descent
chapters.summary: Ossa's POV. Ministry divers breach the ruins; Ossa holds the flooded gate alone with salvaged fireworks and stubbornness, buying the others time. Emotional beat: sacrifice without martyrdom—she expects to survive, and fights like it.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reading the final verses by dragon-light, Wren realizes the prophecy never said Coral must restore the kingdom—it said he must end it. The door out only opens for someone willing to let go. Emotional beat: the trap of destiny revealed as a test of surrender.

chapters.title: Mother's Voice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. His mother's ghost appears in the throne room, still commanding him to reign over a drowned court. Coral refuses her for the first time in his life, naming himself—not Xanthe, not exile, but Coral. Emotional beat: the break from inherited identity.

chapters.title: Unmaking
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The Ministry's chief Unmaker arrives to erase the dragon-fire and the last proof of the Hollow. Coral duels her amid collapsing halls, learning that his storms answer intention, not anger. Emotional beat: mastery earned through acceptance, not domination.

chapters.title: The Door
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With the fire guttering to embers, Coral speaks the closing words of the prophecy and the door out of the dead country opens—a seam of dawn light in the water. He must walk through before the fire dies or be sealed in forever. Emotional beat: threshold terror; leaving means grieving.

chapters.title: What Burns Last
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren carries the dying ember of dragon-fire through the door so something of the Hollow survives—not its throne, but its warmth. The kingdom goes dark behind them, at peace. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into carrying.

chapters.title: Ashgrove Road
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Back in Vell, the Ministry closes in for a final reckoning—but the ghost-court's testimony, delivered through the ember, shames the Unmaker into standing down. Coral surrenders his charms license and registers his magic openly. Emotional beat: visibility chosen, not forced.

chapters.title: A Book Rewritten
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the archive, the self-writing book finishes its last page: no more prophecy, only a record of what was. Wren catalogs it under a new heading—history. Emotional beat: closure; the future is unwritten again.

chapters.title: Storm-Clear
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral calls a gentle rain over Vell's drought-struck gardens, his first public magic, cheered instead of feared. He and Wren plant the dragon-fire ember in a forge where it will warm the city for generations. Emotional beat: belonging—the exile becomes a keeper.

chapters.title: Xanthe and the Hollow
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, coda. Years later, Coral tells children the story of the country that chose to end, signing his name with both names at last: Coral Xanthe Sandoval. Wren's hand rests on the finished book. Emotional beat: peace—inheritance kept by letting go, love kept by staying.
